title: Popup Clearance Approval Modal Observation
claim: FP-MCP-271 records direct operator screenshot evidence of the actual popup-mediated clearance approval modal and finds it partially informative but not compliant with FP-MCP-269: it summarizes clearance creation, workspace, commit, and non-execution, but does not visibly present the full required scope tuple or eliminate Always allow for clearance-creating tools.
summary: The operator captured mobile screenshots of the actual forgepilot_create_operator_local_execution_clearance approval modal after invoking the stale FP-MCP-233 clearance tuple and then denying the request. The modal title was generic: Allow ChatGPT to use ForgePilot MCP? The summary stated that it creates a short-lived operator-local execution clearance artifact for ForgePilot using provided execution and approval packet IDs, workspace 'forgepilot', and commit '2ad7ad1'; it also stated no execution is started and only a local clearance file is written. This is better than the baseline terminal popup because it gives a clearance-specific summary and names workspace, commit, and non-execution. However, it still falls short of FP-MCP-269: the visible main surface does not show the full required tuple, including requestId, approvalPacketId, modelId, runMode, branch, executionBaseCommit/requestArtifactCommit distinction, expiry timestamp/countdown, approval consumption status, disable-switch state, or complete side-effect checklist. The modal remains scroll-heavy on mobile and includes Deny, Allow once, and Always allow. Always allow is unacceptable for clearance-creating tools under FP-MCP-269 unless the platform prevents it or an explicit risk exception is recorded. The actual tool path was declined; no clearance was created.
caveats: This result is based on operator-supplied screenshots of the mobile ChatGPT approval modal, not an automated UI introspection API.
The screenshots are conversation evidence and are summarized here as observations; the image files themselves are not copied into the ForgePilot repo by this checkpoint.
The observed modal may reflect current ChatGPT mobile UI behavior and may change over time.
The modal is partially informative and clearance-specific, so it is not a generic rubber stamp; however, it is not sufficient for FP-MCP-269 compliance.
The presence of Always allow is a serious concern for clearance-creating tools; if the platform cannot suppress it, future FP-027 work requires explicit risk exception and compensating controls.
The operator denied the popup, and the MCP tool result reported the path was declined; no clearance creation occurred.
